nodes.title: Martin’s prime-power correction table
nodes.statement: Define localTerms(p,e) in Q^5, ordered (s,v∞,v2,v3,m), with e=0 giving (1,1,1,1,1). For a prime p and e≥1: s is 1−1/p for e=1, 1−1/p−1/p² for e=2, and (1−1/p)(1−1/p²) for e≥3. v∞ is 0 for odd e, p−2 for e=2, and p^(e/2−2)(p−1)² for even e≥4. For v2, at p=2 the values for e=1,2,3 are −1,−1,1 and thereafter 0; at odd p≡1 mod4 they are 0,−1 and thereafter 0; at odd p≡3 mod4 they are −2,1 and thereafter 0. For v3, at p=3 the values for e=1,2,3 are −1,−1,1 and thereafter 0; at p≡1 mod3 they are 0,−1 and thereafter 0; at p≡2 mod3 they are −2,1 and thereafter 0. m=−1 for e=1 and 0 for e≥2. For nonprime p and e>0 set the whole vector to zero. These are one finite table, not new factorization or modular-form carriers.
hypotheses: p,e are natural numbers; the prime-power interpretation requires p prime.
proofSteps: Use the displayed finite case distinctions and rational arithmetic; exponent zero is treated before the primality test.
acceptance: Retain the exceptional primes 2 and 3; omitting their exponent-three entries changes the dimension formula.

proofSteps: For each prime power check 0≤s≤1−1/p from the three s cases. Multiply these inequalities and use the totient product formula.

proofSteps: If both nonzero rational numbers b and a²−4b are nonsquares, there is an element of the Galois group of their quadratic compositum acting nontrivially on both square roots. This also holds when the two quadratic fields coincide.
